cards.explanation: The answer is demons. Luke says Jesus "…gave them power and authority over all demons…" (Luke 9:1). Notice that word "all," friends. He doesn't hand over a little, He hands over authority over every single one.
The answer is True. Luke 9:1 says Jesus gave the Twelve authority over all demons "…and power to cure diseases." So it's a two-part gift, friends, and both parts come in the same verse.

The answer is the kingdom of God. Jesus "…sent them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick." (Luke 9:2). Two jobs in one sentence, friends. They talk about the kingdom, and they heal the sick.

The answer is False. Jesus told them, "Take nothing for the journey…" and He listed "…no bread, no money…" right there (Luke 9:3). Bread and money stay home, friends. I would have been checking my pockets twice.

The answer is until they leave that area. Jesus says, "Whatever house you enter, stay there until you leave that area." (Luke 9:4). So they stay put in one house, friends, instead of hopping around town looking for a nicer one.

The answer is to shake the dust off their feet. Jesus says, "…shake the dust off your feet when you leave that town, as a testimony against them." (Luke 9:5). That's the instruction for a town that doesn't welcome them, bakers. The dust comes off their feet as they leave.

The answer is from village to village. Luke says they "…went from village to village, preaching the gospel and healing people everywhere." (Luke 9:6). So they're out in the small places, friends, one stop after another.
The answer is puzzled. Luke 9:7 says Herod "was perplexed." Puzzled and perplexed are twins, friends, and he's scratching his head over all the reports about Jesus.

The answer is Elijah. Luke 9:8 says others were saying "…Elijah had appeared…" People were tossing several names into the mix, bakers. Some said John had risen from the dead, and still others said a prophet of old had arisen (Luke 9:7, 8).

The answer is who this man is. Herod says, "I beheaded John…" and then asks, "but who is this man I hear such things about?" (Luke 9:9). He's got a pile of rumors and not one clear answer, friends. The text adds that he kept trying to see Jesus.
The answer is True. The passage ends with this line: "And he kept trying to see Jesus." (Luke 9:9). Not once, either, friends. The words "kept trying" tell you he didn't give up.
